notes: Abel: characterise what to watch for across gain steps from ~unity to absurdly high, one continuous board run (6 stages, 2s settle at baseline=0.2 + 8s watch per stage) rather than 6 restarts. Clear transition: gain 1.0-1.5 grows slowly over seconds and never arms within the 8s window (matches the earlier isolated 1.3 trial); gain>=2.0 grows explosively, arms in 45-84ms, and immediately hits the -6dBFS ceiling. CAVEAT, not a clean result on its own: only 2s settle between back-to-back stages means the higher-gain stages likely re-amplify residual ringing from the previous stage rather than starting from a truly cold, silent baseline each time -- this plausibly explains why 5.0 and 10.0 armed fast here but the earlier ISOLATED, fresh-start 5.0 trial (see detector-jump-latency-v3-dta120-100pct.json) did not arm at all in 3s and was broadband (dominance=6.8dB). Did not attempt to slice/analyse this recording per-stage offline -- the wav is 135.6s against ~60s of active script time (board was already recording before the script connected), so stage boundaries in the file are not precisely known; the timing conclusions above come from the live pybela poll, which IS precisely timed against each trigger. Net finding: once a jump is large/fast enough, the detector catches it quickly (though 45-84ms is a bit over the <25ms budget in ground-rules 7); it is specifically the realistic, near-unity, clean single-partial case (gain 1.0-1.5 here, matching the earlier isolated 1.3 trial) where it currently misses -- reinforcing the kArmGrowthDbPerFrame miscalibration already flagged, not a new finding on its own.
